title: answer/v1
description: What a rail verb answers with --json. `answer` is the shape every answer has. `codes` names every reason.code of an answer that worked: who may own it, the kinds of action it may carry, and the keys of action.facts when it has facts. `error` is the answer of a command that was refused. A brief is written from the facts alone, so a host can read a fact where it would have parsed a sentence. The parts under answer, facts and $defs are JSON Schema.

kind.description: script: run `command`. agent_task: an agent does the brief. person_wait: a person acts. rest: nothing to do.

model.description: On an agent_task for a ticket: the model the tier's ladder names.

facts.description: The values the brief is made of; `codes` says which keys a code has.

guide.description: The [guides] page whose text ends the brief.

ticket_file.description: The ticket's file, from the root of its branch.

shared_facts.description: On every answer with facts that is about one ticket.

adopted.description: From rail adopt: the branch whose work the ticket holds and that branch's head. The brief opens with it.

guide.description: The text of the [guides] page for the brief's situation. The brief ends with it.

consult.description: What consult advised in this same command. The brief ends with it, after the guide.

added_facts.description: What is put around a brief, on any answer with facts.

ACCEPT_AUTO.says: A ticket that passes lint, of a kind approve_contract does not name: next accepts it.

ADOPT.says: rail adopt read a branch and hands over a ticket draft.

ADOPT_CHECKS.says: rail adopt: the draft's checks do not show the work.

ADOPT_SETUP_FAILED.says: rail adopt: setup failed, and nothing was created.

AFTER_DROPPED.says: A ticket this one comes after was dropped: an agent decides whether it still stands.

ANSWER_FINDINGS.says: The review left blocking findings open.

APPROVE_AMEND.says: The contract changed after acceptance in a way a person approves.

APPROVE_CONTRACT.says: The contract of a PERSON ticket whose kind approve_contract names waits for a person's approval.

BUDGET.says: The ticket's runs reported more than [worker] ticket_usd since a person last acted.

spent_by.description: Dollars by what ran: each worker model, each review step.

BUDGET_DAY.says: The runs of the last 24 hours reported more than [worker] daily_usd.

CI_NO_TICKET.says: rail ci on a pull request with no ticket.

CI_WAIT.says: The ticket shipped and CI runs. As a script, a command that waits for the run.

CLAIM.says: An accepted ticket: next claims it.

CONFLICT.says: The pull request conflicts with the base branch.

conflicted.description: The files a merge of the base would conflict in, as far as git can say.

CONSULT.says: A step failed the same way [retry] budget times: next asks consult.

CONTRACT_ELSEWHERE.says: Another session is writing this ticket's contract.

CONTRACT_MERGED.says: A person merged the contract's pull request: next takes it as the approval.

DOCTOR.says: rail doctor: a rest when everything is in place, else what a person fixes.

DROP_PENDING.says: The ticket is dropped and its mark is not written yet.

FORGE_UNAVAILABLE.says: The ticket shipped and GitHub can't be reached.

GITHUB_LIMIT.says: GitHub's rate limit is used up: a wait the script sleeps through, or a rest until it lifts.

GO.says: A person's rail:go is on the ticket: next reads it.

HOLD.says: A person holds the ticket with the label rail:hold.

decided.description: The rows decided when the ticket was written, and not checked.

done_contract.description: The Done Contract section as written, and the command of each Check: line.

base_green.description: Every check of the contract already passed on the base before any work.

out_of_scope.description: The ticket's ## Out of scope, or an empty string.

size.description: The change's size against [size] cap, on an AUTO ticket.

save_note.description: No hook saves for this session, so the brief tells the agent to run rail save.

restarted.description: Until the next ship: the branch the engine replaced with this one, started again from the base, and the scan's rule and file of the secret its commits held.

INIT_TASK.says: The project's config is not on the base branch yet: the init task.

cloud.description: A cloud session, where the agent sets up and a person confirms by merging one pull request.

tools.description: What looks like a tool, as one line.

profiles.description: The language profiles found, as one line.

MERGE.says: A shipped ticket the engine merges: rail advance does it.

MERGE_BY_PERSON.says: A PERSON ticket is ready: a person reviews and merges it.

remote.description: The project has a remote, so the merge is a pull request's.

asked.description: What the reviewer found that a revert doesn't undo, each as kind: file:line: why.

MERGE_FAILED.says: A requested merge has not landed, or GitHub or git refused it (then from rail advance, with no facts).

MERGE_REQUESTED.says: The merge is requested and GitHub has not landed it yet.

PROVISION.says: In a cloud session the project's provision command has not run on this machine.

PROVISIONED.says: rail provision ran, or had run already.

PROVISION_LOCAL.says: rail provision on a person's own machine installs nothing.

REBASE_BEHIND.says: A shipped pull request is behind its base: next rebases it.

REBASING.says: A rebase is stopped in the ticket's worktree.

conflicted.description: The files the rebase stopped on.

RED_BASE.says: verify fails on the base branch too: the ticket waits for the base's fix.

RED_CHECK.says: A required check failed on the pull request.

checks.description: Each failed check and what it printed.

RESTART.says: A person has rotated the secret: next starts the ticket's branch again from the base, under a new name.

RESUME.says: Work an ended session left: next resumes it here.

RETRY_CAP.says: A PERSON ticket is at the retry budget or cap.

could_not_run.description: The capped steps whose last attempt could not run.

REVERT.says: A revert ticket an agent undoes by hand.

REVERT_SHIP.says: A revert ticket whose worktree holds the exact reverse: the ship is all that is left.

REVIEW.says: A shipped patch that needs a review run: rail advance starts it.

SCOPE_OVERLAP.says: Another ticket in flight changes the same paths.

SECRET_FOUND.says: A triage run judged that a line the change adds to .gitleaksignore covers a real secret: a person rotates it, and the engine then starts the ticket's branch again from the base.

question.description: The question's id in the journal.

finding.description: What the line's fingerprint names: the scan's rule, the file and line, the commit. Empty for a line in another form.

SETUP_FAILED.says: The setup command failed in the ticket's worktree.

SOURCE.says: rail source ran a source's fetch: an agent files tickets from what it found.

SOURCES.says: rail source with no name lists the sources.

SOURCE_FULL.says: The source has as many open tickets as it may.

SPLIT.says: An AUTO change over [size] cap is offered a split, once.

rest_branch.description: The branch the brief asks the rest to be moved to.

remote.description: The remote to push that branch to, when the project has one.

STEP_FAILED.says: The last ship failed at a step and nothing has changed since. From rail advance, the answer shows the failure's output as it happened and has no facts.

output.description: What the failed step printed, when this clone kept it.

tried.description: The ticket's ## Tried lines. For a failure of the work itself.

advice.description: Consult's latest advice, while the attempt it was given for is still to come.

triage.description: When the step is triage: the question, the fact that raised it, the answer that stopped the change with what it means, the run's reason, and what the worker is told to do.

STOPPED.says: A person's brake is on: an open issue labelled rail:stop, for this ticket or, with no ticket, for the repository.

STUCK.says: An AUTO ticket at the retry budget or cap: next drops it with a record.

STUCK_REVIEW.says: A review run, or a triage run, failed twice in a row with no verdict.

run.description: The step of the run that last failed.

SWEEP.says: Enough merged since the last sweep: rail sweep.

SWEEP_EMPTY.says: A sweep that found nothing: it ships and merges.

SWEEP_RUN.says: A sweep ticket whose review run is still to come.

SWEEP_TICKETS.says: The sweep ran: an agent files its findings as tickets.

TICKET_LINT.says: The ticket is not complete: an agent writes its contract. From rail add and rail amend, the file given did not pass lint, and the answer has no facts.

not_taken.description: Why an issue that held a whole ticket was taken as a request only.

TOOL_DOWN.says: A step failed for the machine's own reason twice in a row: a tool out of reach, or a command that could not run.

TOOL_MISSING.says: A declared tool has no credential on this machine. One ticket's wait, or with `tickets` the one wait of several.

tools_missing.description: Each tool and the names it lacks.

machine.description: The kind of machine, which says where a name is set.

tickets.description: The tickets the wait holds, when the answer is about several.

resting.description: What else rests, one line a ticket, when the answer is about several.

TRIAGE.says: A question the engine raised about the shipped patch has no answer: rail advance starts the triage run, before any review.

VERIFY_ASSUMPTIONS.says: The ticket has open ASSUMED rows to verify before the work.

WAITING_AFTER.says: The ticket waits for a ticket in `after` to merge.

WAITING_PERSON.says: No agent has work, and tickets wait for a person.

waits.description: Each wait, with its own brief.

resting.description: What else rests, one line a ticket.

WORKED.says: rail work ran the worker once: rail advance is next.

pr.description: The ticket's pull request, or null when it has none.

kind.description: approval: of something a revert doesn't undo, money included. grant: the machine lacks something a person gives once, or something outside the repository is a person's to do. hold: the person's own brake.

accept.description: The command that approves or continues: rail accept NN. A note may follow it in quotes.

label.description: The label that does the same on the ticket's open pull request: rail:go.

drop.description: The command that ends the ticket instead.

answer.description: The command with which the person decides a finding; F1 stands for the finding's id.

amend.description: The command that changes the ticket instead.

merge.description: The pull request a person reviews and merges.

issue.description: The rail:stop issue: closing it, or taking the label off, ends the wait.

set.description: The names of the environment variables to set on the machine; then rail next.

wait.description: What a person's wait asks, and each way to answer it that works here.

finding.description: A review finding as the journal holds it, and its last answer once it has one.

findings.description: The blocking findings still to answer, then the open advisory ones. Empty while no blocking finding is open.

failed.description: The failed step's event: its name, how it ended, and the signature of its output.

stuck.description: Each step at its limit: cap ([retry] cap failures of any kind), same (the same failure [retry] budget times in a row), consulted (once more after consult advised).

revert.description: A revert ticket: the ticket it reverts and that ticket's squash commit, whether the worktree holds the exact reverse, whether the reverse still applies to the base, and whether verify failed on it.

history.description: What earlier work on the same paths left: the last merged tickets and the markers standing there.

stop.description: The open issue labelled rail:stop, and the paths it names when it stops only those.

person_note.description: What a person said with their last approval or continue, until the next ship.

cwd.description: The ticket's worktree, from the project's root.
